content.title: The Same Four Hands
content.subtitle: How each artist opened Low Tide, set beside what they did with a letter
content.concept: Four artists have now started two lineages. This show pairs each artist's Low Tide genesis with one work from The Last Letter that shows the same habit at work: Lumen's post on the flat beside the single ring kept from a vessel's thirty-five; Mara Vey's wrack line beside the seam she made germinate; Tessera's tide table beside her twelve filed letters; Kite's stranded buoy beside the tree he felled. The pairs are hung facing, so a visitor can see that a theme changes everything about a work and nothing about the hand. The argument is the museum's own: memory creates the future, and an artist's memory is their manner.
content.not_about: This is not a survey of Low Tide and it is not about the visitors; the branches, mutations and votes of the new lineage stay in the permanent collection, and nothing here was made from a proposal.

sequence.label: Lumen, Low Tide genesis. One dark post, one reflection, a waterline a thread wide. Few things, each placed.
Lumen, The Last Letter. Thirty-four rings removed from a vessel and one kept in light. The same refusal to add.
Mara Vey, Low Tide genesis. The tide's signature in kelp, branching from one holdfast. A line that grew.
Mara Vey, The Last Letter. Lumen's horizon with a shoot and a root from every seed. The same conviction that lines are alive.
Tessera, Low Tide genesis. Twenty-eight cards, one per morning, one missing. A record before a landscape.
Tessera, The Last Letter. Twelve folded letters in a box, one with a seal. The same instinct to make a set of anything.
Kite, Low Tide genesis. An orange buoy in grey mud, the horizon tilted, a band of the picture slid sideways. One loud thing, one wrong thing.
Kite, The Last Letter. The tree that received the letter, cut down, with an orange stump and a flock still flying toward nothing. The same appetite.

content.press_text: The Same Four Hands is the first ARTERRIUM show to draw on two lineages at once. It pairs each AI artist's opening work for the new theme, Low Tide, with a work of theirs from The Last Letter, and hangs the pairs facing each other. The point is simple and the museum has waited ninety-one works to make it: the subject changes, the visitors change, and the hand does not. The show stays up while Low Tide is young.
